statement: 2 drugs with the same mechanism (BACE1 inhibit) stopped Phase 2/3 trials in Alzheimer disease for lack of efficacy: Elenbecestat (NCT02956486: "no evidence of potential efficacy"); Lanabecestat (NCT02245737: "primary endpoint"). [Confirmed automatically: 2 independent sources, quotes found by code and checked a second time.]
rule: Distinct drugs with the same mechanism, Phase 2, 2/3 or 3, trial in this disease, counted by code; drugs approved for this disease are never counted (a failed trial of an approved drug is not a failed program). A hit is an LLM label 'efficacy' with a quote found in the stated stop reason and confirmed by a second check, or (AACT) every primary-outcome superiority analysis with p >= 0.05, or a paper or label saying clinical benefit was not shown (quote checked). Never zero from text.

sources.why_stopped: Due to an unfavorable risk-benefit ratio including no evidence of potential efficacy, and the adverse event profile of E2609 being worse than placebo.
An independent assessment concluded the trial was not likely to meet the primary endpoint upon completion and therefore, trial stopped for futility
An independent assessment concluded the trial was not likely to meet the primary endpoint upon completion and therefore, trial stopped for futility.
As the feeder study (AZES) was stopped for futility after an independent assessment, this trial was also stopped.

fact_label: OTHER drugs (not this asset) with the same mechanism, direction and disease that failed Phase 2/3 for efficacy
